out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. CDI: PIC LABELED THE CHEMICAL SPRAY BOTTLES WITH BRAND NAMES.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: DRESSING SQUEEZE BOTTLE AND CONTAINERS OF SEASONINGS IN THE DRY STORAGE AREA.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. ENSURE ALL FOOD CONTAINERS ARE LABELED BY THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. OBSERVED PACKAGED FOODS IN THE WALK IN FREEZER AND DRY STORAGE FOOD STORED ON THE FLOOR
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. ENSURE ALL FOODS ARE OFF THE FLOOR BY THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following equipment is not operating properly and/or is in poor repair: LEAK AT THE HVAC VENT IN THE WALK IN COOLER.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. ENSURE WALK IN COOLER IS IN GOOD REPAIR BY THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION. El Sabor Boliviano (Inspection Date: 09/16/2026) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Equip/Utensils, Durable under Normal Use
violations.observation: The following equipment is not designed and constructed to be durable: GROCERY BAGS USED TO STORE BEEF IN THE WALK IN COOLER AND NON- GRADE CONTAINERS USED TO STORE DRY GOODS.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment and utensils shall be designed and constructed to be durable and to retain their characteristic qualities under normal use conditions. ENSURE ALL FOODS ARE STORED IN FOOD GRADE MATERIALS BY THE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Toilet facilities properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned

violations.title: Toilet Room, Kept Closed
violations.observation: Observed that the employee toilet room door in the kitchen is kept open.
violations.corrective_action: Keep toilet room doors closed to prevent insect and rodent entrance and the associated spread of potential disease. CDI: PIC CLOSED THE RESTROOM DOOR.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: RAW SHELL EGGS STORED OVER PREPARED SAUCES IN TURBO AIR 3 DOOR PREP TOP.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC REORGANIZED FOODS DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. RICE AT 44F IN DEEP COVERED CONTAINER PREPARED THE PREVIOUS DAY IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO DISCARD FOODS DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE PROPER COOLING METHODS ARE USED TO RAPIDLY COOL FOODS FROM 135F TO 70F IN 2 HOURS AND TO A FURTHER 41F WITHIN A TOTAL OF 6 HOURS. El Sabor Boliviano (Inspection Date: 03/23/2026) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: CHICKEN BROTH AT 113F ON STOVE TOP.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO HAVE FOODS REHEATED TO 165F OR ABOVE DURING INSPECTION FOR HOT HOLDING AT 135F OR ABOVE.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: RICE AT 44F IN DEEP COVERED CONTAINER PREPARED THE PREVIOUS DAY IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO DISCARD FOODS DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE USE SMALLER PORTIONS, SHALLOW PANS IN FREEZER OR REFRIGERATOR TO RAPIDLY COOL FOODS TO THE PROPER COOLING PARAMETERS.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: Hard boiled eggs in 3DR prep top unit were temping at 50F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL COLD HOLDING FOODS MUST BE KEPT AT A MAXIMUM TEMPERATURE OF 41F OR BELOW. EGGS HAD ONLY BEEN IN COOLER FOR AN HOUR. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE MOVE EGGS TO COLD HOLDING UNIT BELOW TO COOL BACK TO 41F.
